Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR preserves authenticated requester identity through delegation, queued execution, and recovery, with opt-in collaborative steering and explicit followup behavior. **Example:** Alice selects accepted participant Bob for a queued child execution. - **Before:** The child could pair Bob’s authority with Alice’s requester facts or lose requester identity during recovery. - **After:** The child retains Bob’s identity, resolves applicable policy at admission, and rejects revoked or reassigned authority before effects. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Useful repair with substantive shipped-entry-point, final-effect, live-channel, and upgrade evidence; unresolved validation failures limit confidence in the integrated candidate. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): The previous four Before-merge items are addressed: real selected-child HTTP/file effects and revoked/reassigned zero-effect outcomes replace the earlier mocked-execution gap; seven live two-human Telegram scenarios exercise authorization and followup behavior; and published v2026.10.4 upgraded state proceeds through selected-requester queueing and cold recovery. Current production matches the exercised parent. Queued revocation is supported compositionally by shared owners and custody tests. Inspector images were directly inspected. Portal retrieval was unavailable here, so execution results are assessed from the detailed source-bound public reports. Rollback restoration, pre-upgrade human-profile continuity, independently varied restart policy, and a performance guarantee are not claimed. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Delegated or recovered work can lose the authenticated requester or combine one person’s authority with another person’s identity. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction accepts the steering and participant-selection contracts, and the implementation addresses a concrete permission and execution-identity problem. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 1 item remains** Keep open: this maintainer-owned repair remains useful, and the updated evidence addresses the previous authority and upgrade blockers; integration validation remains outstanding. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `d3ddc954302f83bf566f99a89f37d6faf7777ad7` ## Before merge - [ ] **Complete next step** - Reconcile the recorded dirty merge state with current main and complete required integration validation, preserving the unresolved CI failures until evidence establishes their cause. ## Findings None.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Authenticated channel and Gateway inputs enter the admission owners, which carry requester facts into queued, delegated, and recovered executions; existing tool and transport owners enforce authority before effects. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Authenticated input] --> B[Requester capture] B --> C[Execution admission] C --> D[Queue and recovery custody] D --> C C --> E[Delegated execution] E --> F[Current authority checks] F --> G[Tool and transport effects] C --> H[Audit receipts] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the existing admission and custody owners, preserve the accepted requester contract, and complete integration validation without weakening authority checks. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Current-main policy resolution consumes persisted delegated projections without this PR’s preserved requester-origin admission path; source inspection and the supplied source-bound behavior reports establish the affected boundary, without executing target code during this review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The inspected implementation uses the existing requester-policy, participant-selection, transcript-custody, and recovery owners, preserves intentional delegation, and supplies the missing final-effect and upgrade evidence. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [806ea5812ccb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/806ea5812ccbe393b4dd0c3a6c1ce0010a5d755a). ### Provenance checked - `Participant selection and native delegation` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160525: Require explicit participant selection after multi-person steering and refuse ambiguous native delegation.) - `Requester completion policy` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160786: Restore a yielded requester’s captured policy through exact completion custody while preserving revocation and final-effect checks.) - `Operator restart recovery` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166553: Re-admit the exact persisted authenticated source under current authority rather than infer privilege from session ownership.) ### Testing Proof path: shipped entry point. ### Security None. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Pinned introduction and unchanged production proof inputs:** Reviewed introduced hunks against b2e85fadecb2d19aa4a501e9729b508c3975eb22. The final commit changes only the membership and updater test fixtures; production inputs match the 42a6bffeeb596554129eb5918b3abfcb2ed83cdf candidate used for the latest live and recovery proof. ([`src/gateway/server.chat-membership-authority.product.test.ts:261`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d3ddc954302f83bf566f99a89f37d6faf7777ad7/src/gateway/server.chat-membership-authority.product.test.ts#L261), [d3ddc954302f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d3ddc954302f83bf566f99a89f37d6faf7777ad7)) - **Selected-child authority proof:** The updated PR body reports five source-bound Gateway scenarios with real child HTTP/file effects after source completion, zero sink writes after unlinking or reassignment during awaited preparation, and retained queued requester custody. Source inspection confirms selection carries authority and requester origin together. Queued revocation remains compositional proof rather than one continuous live trace. ([`src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-gateway.ts:57`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d3ddc954302f83bf566f99a89f37d6faf7777ad7/src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-gateway.ts#L57), [d3ddc954302f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d3ddc954302f83bf566f99a89f37d6faf7777ad7)) - **Live Telegram authorization:** Josh Avant’s detailed [live report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157806#issuecomment-6254936495) correlates real human ingress, runtime refusals, followup notices, execution identities, writes, denied writes, and terminal ingress records across seven scenarios, including the moved direct-policy callback. ([`extensions/telegram/src/security.ts:53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/42a6bffeeb596554129eb5918b3abfcb2ed83cdf/extensions/telegram/src/security.ts#L53), [42a6bffeeb59](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/42a6bffeeb596554129eb5918b3abfcb2ed83cdf)) - **Upgrade and cold-recovery composition:** The updated body and [maintainer report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157806#issuecomment-6255533594) describe a published v2026.10.4 upgrade followed by selected-Bob queued work and actual cold recovery using the installed candidate package and upgraded state. Include-owned true, old history/session identity, FIFO, exactly-once execution, and withdrawal survived. The released profile catalog was empty; policy was not independently varied across restart. ([`src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/42a6bffeeb596554129eb5918b3abfcb2ed83cdf/src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.ts), [42a6bffeeb59](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/42a6bffeeb596554129eb5918b3abfcb2ed83cdf)) - **Compatibility and accepted scope:** The maintainer-authored direction explicitly accepts incumbent authority for unqualified operations, opt-in cross-person steering, and selected-participant delegation. Legacy prepared channel policies retain their original-request snapshot contract through a documented deprecation adapter. Older receipt-reader limitations and unsuccessful rollback observations remain disclosed. Public docs: [`docs/plugins/sdk-migration/compatibility-policy.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/compatibility-policy). ([`docs/plugins/sdk-migration/compatibility-policy.md:46`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-migration/compatibility-policy), [d3ddc954302f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d3ddc954302f83bf566f99a89f37d6faf7777ad7)) - **Inspector media inspected:** Directly inspected the body’s GitHub-hosted before/after images. The after image adds Recorded authority subject while retaining unknown outcome and unverified provenance. The prepared manifest contained only expired, unrelated plugin-installation images returning HTTP 403; scratch-file downloads were blocked, so the current inspector images were inspected from fetched bytes. ([`ui/src/pages/activity/run-inspector-evidence-view.tsx:207`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d3ddc954302f83bf566f99a89f37d6faf7777ad7/ui/src/pages/activity/run-inspector-evidence-view.tsx#L207), [d3ddc954302f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d3ddc954302f83bf566f99a89f37d6faf7777ad7)) ### PR surface PR surface statistics unavailable: the file list is incomplete. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **New configuration option** | 1 boolean; default false | messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering explicitly controls cross-person influence over an incumbent execution; Doctor preserves explicit stored values. | ### Labels Label changes: - add `proof: sufficient`: Contributor real behavior proof is sufficient. - add `rating: 🐚 platinum hermit`: Overall readiness is 🐚 platinum hermit; proof is 🐚 platinum hermit and patch quality is 🐚 platinum hermit. - add `status: ⏳ waiting on author`: ClawSweeper has contributor-facing work open and is waiting for author action. - remove `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`: Current PR rating is `rating: 🐚 platinum hermit`, so this older rating label is no longer current. - remove `status: 📣 needs proof`: Current PR status label is `status: ⏳ waiting on author`. Label justifications: - `P1`: Incorrect requester identity affects established delegation, permission enforcement, and recovered agent workflows. - `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`: The accepted change alters default steering behavior and adds a channel SDK callback while retaining a documented legacy-policy compatibility path. - `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary`: The accepted design transfers selected human authority into detached children and permits cross-person steering only through explicit opt-in; final-effect revocation proof now covers the changed selection path. - `rating: 🐚 platinum hermit`: Overall readiness is 🐚 platinum hermit; proof is 🐚 platinum hermit and patch quality is 🐚 platinum hermit. - `status: ⏳ waiting on author`: ClawSweeper has contributor-facing work open and is waiting for author action. - `proof: sufficient`: Contributor real behavior proof is sufficient. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab. Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality; ✨ marks media proof (a screenshot, video, or linked artifact) that directly shows the changed behavior. ### Workflow ClawSweeper edits this one comment on every review. ## Retained validation history through `0f38dbd9e4`

These observations retain their original source, failure, and cost qualifications. They are historical evidence, not a verdict on later commits. Current behavior, proof, and remaining gaps are in the PR description.

## Current validation

Published head **`0f38dbd9e491b14c86b412e3d8508e87af3e824d`**, rebased once onto `2f228582f354803021c3d217d3a2fd79b54b0305`. All 36 commits retain authorship/order; 34 reapplied unchanged. Three conflicts preserve main's MCP/TUI consolidation and branch assertions, then regenerate config hashes. Main's new MCP fixture receives its required prepared-policy field. No manual production conflict edits. Source audits/scoped AutoReview: no P0–P2 findings (0.99); 57 proof postimages match committed blobs. Clean worktree; **MERGEABLE**, open, no auto-merge.

[Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38798270715): **146 successful, 20 skipped, 5 failed jobs** (four shards plus gate), merge `f0492e5f` / main `591db854`. Memory-owner and Doctor invalid-ownership failures are source-attributed inherited, without fresh baseline reproduction. Two timeout causes remain **unresolved**. [Doctor replay](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_486c4db064ef38e74aa16340176f6551): 19/19 each, 172.551/176.205 s. Gateway [main](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e3e87e4c27f6393abe98571d68effd80) / [CI merge](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9a7fce836bc30495135f0adbadb885a3): 101/101 each, 247.308/246.759 s. Both timeouts were **not reproduced**; passes prove neither a fix nor unrelatedness. Original order/limits retained; sources, logs and settlement verified. No safe branch repair identified; no CI rerun/re-push or green claim. AWS cleanup independently confirmed complete.

The [rebase proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c11cdaf8e7e8d95b27cc654bdfe6f719) passed **156/156, zero skipped/pending/todo**; all 15 commands settled without cleanup signals. Frozen install, runtime build (**92.728 s**), native type leaves (**144.728 s** combined), lint (**23.367 s**), format and diff passed. Canonical config generation/check (**6.165 / 5.665 s**) yields core **2,519**, retaining main's new leaf and the approved setting. Archive/log/report/postimage reconciliation passed. Initial manifest sync lacked Git and failed before commands; the existing synthetic-checkout recipe repaired that prerequisite on the same lease. Failed evidence remains; no assertions changed. AWS cleanup independently confirmed complete.

| Rebase file | Result | `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall (s) | AWS case-seconds | CI case-seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

All four blobs match the CI merge and all 156 cases pass there. CI case-seconds sum native displayed timings; isolated CI file-wrapper times are unavailable. Provenance's group passed inside a later-failed job. Required complete job logs were CRC/size/hash-verified from an interrupted archive; that transport failure remains recorded. AWS/CI timings are not an isolated performance comparison. Historical proof below retains its original source qualification.

Source reviews 5/6 were scoped-clean. Review 7's original P2/incorrect verdict remains declined on source evidence: TUI `agentCommandFromIngress` reaches the embedded attempt, not the auto-reply queue-directive writer; built-in names remain reserved from skill expansion. That disposition is not a runtime or CI verdict.

The retained pre-rebase [final single-fixture proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a6e2d51321730a7651881d92ec2998ad) verified the intended old-code failure and current full-file pass: **3P/0F/0skip, 54.521 s wrapper / 14.093364 case-seconds**. With the same fixture, old95 fails exactly because injection occurred once at assertion 166 (**0P/1F, two filtered; 64.374 s wrapper / 9.306387 case-seconds**), not by timeout. All 12 commands settled: 11 exited 0 and that intended negative exited 1. Gateway-methods types (**14.366 s**), lint (**16.033 s**), format and diff passed; 112 source hashes and baseline cleanup verified. The fixture publishes canonical config and observes injection before dispatch, preserving its three cases, 46 assertions and timeouts. Production and 111 other files are unchanged from the correction. This closes the selected primary proof, not full PR CI or earlier failed attempts. The [broad continuation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_91cdf48d8d725c6d89c4ae3ea6b87d8b) is **incomplete**: eight full files **701P/1F of 702**, zero skipped/pending/todo. Format, diff and baseline cleanup passed. Repairs use the canonical disposition type and move compaction-notice preparation to the existing presentation owner. Broad lint and the 239-case runner consumer passed; broad TUI type failures were cleared by the correction.
- Initial final-delta stopped before tests: build exit 0 (**90.119 s**), then remaining process-group membership triggered cleanup and harness failure. Source receipts were unchanged; child identity was unobserved, so no product cause is assigned.

Proof1 has archive-bound native JSON/command logs but no producer member manifest or independent final-source/quiescence receipt. Reached final hash assertions do not manufacture those receipts; later receipts qualify only their own runs.

Approved canonical generation/check passed (**7 / 5 s**, 14 s elapsed), preserving all 99 inputs and producing the adopted counts/snapshot/hash; core count **2,518**. Broad schema-help **3P** cost **4.265 s wrapper / 0.007777 case-seconds**; config-docs passed in **5.766 s**.

Both investigations used two workers (original recovery CI: eight), Node 24.21 versus CI 24.19, and omitted the preceding separate 12-file child. Console totals supply no per-case JSON or standalone cost.

The real Gateway test crosses ingress, execution authority, foreground delivery, durable custody and Bob's explicit followup/current policy. Seven live Telegram behavior scenarios passed on `42a6bffeeb596554129eb5918b3abfcb2ed83cdf` (tree `89ebf9ee3f1eea138761ed987f37594f7339fd84`).

This used two existing human Telegram clients, one private test topic, and an isolated exact-candidate Gateway on direct AWS Crabbox. Actual Telegram ingress established distinct numeric senders, both `is_bot:false`, with no anonymous/channel sender. Provider responses were scripted to control timing; channel admission, native execution, tools, transport responses, audit records and filesystem effects were real. There was no Convex credential use or human-session export.

| Scenario | Actual Telegram correlation | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Setting omitted | A17, B18; refusal19 | B’s natural-language stop received the exact runtime refusal. A’s execution remained unchanged and completed a real write. |
| Explicit false | A21, B22, A24; refusal23 | B’s `/steer stop ...` was refused. A24 was injected into the original A execution (`active_run_injected`), followed by a successful write. |
| Busy `/followup` | A26, B27; queued28; replies29/30 | Runtime acknowledged actual queue acceptance. Bob’s global write policy changed before drain, without a channel restart. His distinct new execution used the changed policy and rejected the attempted write. |
| Idle `/followup` | B31; started32; reply33 | A new Bob execution received the exact started notice, rejected the forbidden write and finished. |
| Explicit true | A34, B35; A reply36 | B35 was injected, preserving Bob’s actual author metadata and Alice’s exact execution identity. Alice could write despite Bob’s deny. Default `sessions_spawn` omitted `user`; the real child had agent invoker and exact Alice parent lineage. It wrote successfully **after Alice’s terminal result**. |
| Bob after collaboration | B38; started39; reply40 | Bob’s new execution still had Bob’s identity and rejected the same write capability. |
| Telegram direct policy | A609/reply610, then A611/reply612 | With global DMs disabled and only A’s exact private conversation enabled, the first admission wrote successfully. After applying the direct sender deny while idle, a distinct admission of the same A rejected the write. |

Message numbers above are actual Telegram message IDs on their indicated group/direct surfaces; private account and conversation identifiers are omitted. The 13 human update IDs were `932434587`–`932434599`. All eleven resulting runs finished successfully: nine human executions, one child and one ordinary child-completion announce wake. The wake explicitly recorded absent invoker/unattributed coverage; it is **not** presented as another human execution or human approval.

After later followups drained, neither refused message became a new native prompt/execution. The exact durable ingress rows for all 13 updates were then read from stopped, immutable databases: one completed tombstone each, nonnull completion time, payload `null`, and cleared claims. No pending-input rows were observed; we do not equate that absence with cancellation or nonexecution. The conclusion combines the actual skipped admission decisions, later run boundaries and settled transport records. Existing recovery/race proofs remain the evidence for duplicate delivery, restart and cancellation mechanics; no new live Telegram replay is claimed.

The proof produced five successful real file writes and four policy-filtered write rejections (`Tool write not found`); forbidden effect files remained absent. Ten stored execution tuples independently matched the observed admissions, keeping A, B and the invoking agent distinct. Source and all nine qualified build artifacts were byte-identical before and after live work.

[Live run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_34d7bb92394edf52959ead2b8d38baac): 589.880 s command / 623.351 s native total. [Storage closeout](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f43445dece99d3022f304219519609f7): 39.604 s command / 91.565 s native total. These are opt-in proof costs, not recurring CI or production-performance measurements. Sanitized proof-summary SHA256: `5d4c0c1503444cf02673aaa29de55e8518d86565e6411bc03fb052c736b2eca2`; stored private receipt SHA256: `8db9d76564d82677725889152bce21a287fd080f7fc6f8b26a79d7feab1c5672`.

Cleanup: the proof Gateway and every observed descendant/process group stopped; the local tunnel and task-owned keep-awake process stopped; both bot command-menu scopes were restored and read back. No competing poller or Telegram API failure was observed. One observer wait used the wrong selector for a marked reply and timed out; the independent outbound receipt verified that reply, with no resend. Tool-free auxiliary requests are strongly consistent with Activity recap, but raw prompts were not retained, so that attribution remains an inference.

This adds live channel and enforcement evidence. It does not establish model judgment quality, human intent, full rollback safety, or a new performance guarantee. The PR remains unmerged.
